title: Smiling and frowning curves: concavity and inflection
examples: What is a point of inflection?
What does the second derivative tell you?

marks.label: Inflection point
marks.ask: What is a point of inflection?

explain.say: A new phone goes on sale in Indonesia. At first few people buy it, then sales rush, then they slow down as most people have one. This curve shows the total sold. Look at the yellow mark: the curve bends upwards, like a smile.

draw.text: Smiling and frowning curves: concavity and inflection

marks.label: Inflection point
marks.ask: What is a point of inflection?

explain.say: Bending up, called concave up, means the slope is getting steeper. More phones sell each week than the week before. The second derivative, the rate of change of the slope, is positive here. Can you see it getting steeper?

marks.label: Inflection point
marks.ask: What is a point of inflection?

explain.say: Now the purple mark. The curve still rises, but it bends downwards, like a frown. That is concave down. Fewer new phones sell each week, so the second derivative is negative.

marks.label: Inflection point
marks.ask: What is a point of inflection?

explain.say: Between them, at the cyan mark, the bending switches from smile to frown. This is the point of inflection. Here the curve is steepest: the week with the most sales. What do you think the second derivative is here?

marks.label: Inflection point
marks.ask: What is a point of inflection?

explain.say: Zero! Great thinking. At an inflection point the second derivative is zero and changes sign. Health experts watch for this point in a spreading illness: it means new cases have started to slow down.

marks.label: Inflection point
marks.ask: What is a point of inflection?

faq.a: A curve is concave up when it bends upwards like a smile or a cup. Its slope keeps increasing, and its second derivative is positive.
A curve is concave down when it bends downwards like a frown or a hill. Its slope keeps decreasing, and its second derivative is negative.
asks: What does a negative second derivative mean?

faq.q: What is a point of inflection?
faq.a: It is where a curve changes from bending one way to bending the other. The second derivative is zero there and changes sign.

faq.q: What does the second derivative tell you?
faq.a: It tells you how the slope is changing. Positive means the curve bends up, negative means it bends down.

faq.q: Why is the inflection point the steepest part here?
faq.a: Before it the slope grows, after it the slope shrinks. So the slope is biggest exactly where it stops growing: the inflection point.
asks: Why do the most sales happen at the inflection point?

facts: At a point of inflection the second derivative is zero and changes sign.
For f(x) = x³, the second derivative 6x is zero at x = 0, which is a point of inflection.

quiz.say: A curve bends up like a smile. Its second derivative is…
quiz.show: A curve bends up like a smile. Its second derivative is…
quiz.why: Concave up means the slope is increasing, so f″ is positive.

wrong.1: Negative second derivative means bending down, like a frown.
wrong.2: Zero happens only at special points like inflections.

quiz.say: f double dash of x equals 6x. Where is the point of inflection?
quiz.show: f″(x) = 6x. Where is the point of inflection?
quiz.why: 6x = 0 at x = 0, and 6x changes sign there.

wrong.0: At x = 6, f″ is 36, not zero.
wrong.2: At x = 1, f″ is 6, not zero.
